llm.summary: This image skill is mostly coherent, but it deserves review because broad triggers can send prompts or local images to dLazy using a locally stored API key.

dimensions.detail: Network calls, local media reads, and uploads are expected for cloud image generation and are disclosed, with local file uploads limited to paths supplied as command inputs.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The install is pinned to npm package @dlazy/cli@1.2.3 and can also run via npx; npm metadata and the package tarball did not show install/postinstall scripts, but the global CLI exposes broader dLazy commands beyond banana2.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger list includes generic image-generation/editing phrases, so ordinary image requests may select this third-party, credit-consuming CLI without a provider-specific user request.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Authentication persists a dLazy API key in ~/.dlazy/config.json; package inspection found ordinary writeFileSync config writes without explicit chmod, despite the skill claiming OS-user-restricted file permissions.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is Nano Banana 2 image generation/editing, and the documented behavior of sending prompts, parameters, and user-specified media to dLazy endpoints fits that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this before installing if you do not want generic image requests routed to dLazy. Use it only when comfortable sending prompts and selected local media to dLazy, and consider using DLAZY_API_KEY per invocation instead of persistent login if local key storage is a concern.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad English trigger terms match the image-generation purpose, but paired with remote uploads and credit usage they create a real accidental-invocation concern.
[SQP-1] expected: The Chinese trigger terms similarly align with the purpose but are generic enough to warrant user review rather than an automatic malicious classification.
